land.text: Sivas, Kayseri, Amasya, Tokat, Çorum, Ürgüp (Nevşehir), Canik, Şebinkarahisar, Niğde, Aksaray, Ankara and Darende: the places the page lists as incorporated, without dates

predecessors.note: Eretna was Timurtash's man and governor of Anatolia; 'With Abu Sa'id's death in 1335, the Ilkhanid period practically came to an end' (Eretnids page). Eretna 'came under the suzerainty of the Jalayirid viceroy of Anatolia, Hasan Buzurg'.

successors.note: 'His regent was Kadi Burhan al-Din, who proclaimed himself as the ruler by January 1381' (Eretnids page); 'In 1381, he took over Eretnid lands and claimed the title of sultan for himself' (Kadi Burhan al-Din page).

capitals.name: Sivas
capitals.note: 'with the capital initially situated in Sivas and later Kayseri' (Eretnids page); neither move is dated. Bridge at confidence 1: Sivas to the death of Eretna in 1352.

capitals.name: Kayseri
capitals.note: Muhammad I 'was murdered by his emirs (vassals) in Kayseri, the capital' (Eretnids page; he reigned 1352-1365). The Kadi Burhan al-Din page instead says 'the initial capital of the Eretnid Beylik was Erzincan, later moving to Kayseri'.

capitals.name: Sivas
capitals.note: 1375: the Karamanids seized Kayseri, 'forcing Alaeddin Ali to flee to Sivas' (Kadi Burhan al-Din page).

capitals.name: Kayseri
capitals.note: 1378: Burhan al-Din 'reclaimed Kayseri and expelled Alaeddin Karamanid'; Ala al-Din Ali died in August 1380 (Eretnids page).

rulers.name: Eretna
rulers.title: sultan
rulers.note: Infobox 1335-1352; 'He first declared his independence in 1341' (first coin with the title sultan); the Eretnids page gives his death as February, March or August 1352.

rulers.name: Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad I
rulers.note: Eretna's son (the page: he allied with the Dulkadirids in September 1362 and was 'murdered by his emirs (vassals) in Kayseri, the capital'; the page dates his death 1365 only in the passage on Niğde and Aksaray). The page also has a ruler 'deposed by his emirs in 1354' and 'his half-brother Jafar' reigning to 1355 without naming the ruler; the strip follows the infobox 1335-1352 and the 1365 murder.

rulers.name: Ala al-Din Ali
rulers.note: Crowned at 13 after his father's murder; 'Ala al-Din Ali died in Kazova in August 1380 from the plague amidst another attempt to crush Shadgeldi'.

rulers.name: Ali's successor under the regent Kadi Burhan al-Din
rulers.note: The infobox has a second period 1380-1381; 'His regent was Kadi Burhan al-Din, who proclaimed himself as the ruler by January 1381'. The extract does not name the child ruler.

correction.text: Sivas, Kayseri, Amasya, Tokat, Çorum, Ürgüp (Nevşehir), Canik, Şebinkarahisar, Niğde, Aksaray, Ankara and Darende: the places the page lists as incorporated, without dates

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Eretnids). The page says the dynasty 'ruled a state spanning central and eastern Anatolia from 1335 to 1381' and that Eretna's realm 'extended from Konya to Ankara and Erzurum, also incorporating Kayseri, Amasya, Tokat, Çorum, Develi, Karahisar, Zile, Canik, Ürgüp, Niğde, Aksaray, Erzincan, Şebinkarahisar, and Darende'. None of the incorporations is dated except Darende (lost 1338-1339), Erzincan (1343), Konya (1350) and the later losses; the places not dated are drawn from 1335. Konya and Erzincan appear later.
New keyframe. 'In 1338-1339, Eretna lost Darende to Qaraja' (Dulkadir).

union.text: Erzincan with Erzurum and Bayburt: the eastern part of the realm

correction.text: the realm with Erzincan and the eastern cities annexed in 1343

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Battle of Karanbük (September-October 1343) 'resulted in the Eretnid annexation of Erzincan and several cities further east'; the eastern part of the realm is later named as Erzincan, Erzurum and Bayburt, so those three are drawn as the 'several cities'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Eretna further took advantage of the Karamanid ruler Ahmed's death in 1350, capturing Konya.'

correction.text: the realm with Erzincan and the eastern cities annexed in 1343

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Konya is dropped again at confidence 1: the page does not say when the Karamanids regained it, and the Karaman dossier has the Karamanids in Konya until 1390.

correction.text: the realm without Ankara (taken by Murad I in 1361)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Murad I captured Ankara Castle from the Eretnids', in 1361 'as a reprisal to a raid by Tatars of the Chavdar tribe'.

correction.text: the realm without Ankara and without Erzincan, Erzurum and Bayburt (Ahi Ayna, about 1365)

correction.text: the realm without Niğde and Aksaray (Karamanid invasion, undated, after 1365)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After Muhammad's 1365 death 'The Karamanids invaded Niğde and Aksaray, and local Mongol tribes started disrupting the public order'. The page does not say the Karamanids kept the towns; they are dropped at confidence 1.

New keyframe. 1375: 'Alaeddin Bey of the Karamanids seized Kayseri, forcing Alaeddin Ali to flee to Sivas' (Kadi Burhan al-Din page; the Eretnids page: 'the Karamanids captured the city with the help of the Mongol tribes').

correction.text: the realm without Niğde and Aksaray (Karamanid invasion, undated, after 1365)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 1378: 'Burhan al-Din reclaimed Kayseri and expelled Alaeddin Karamanid' while serving the Eretnid ruler as vizier.

region.text: Sivas, Kayseri, Amasya, Tokat, Çorum, Ürgüp (Nevşehir), Canik, Şebinkarahisar, Niğde, Aksaray, Ankara and Darende: the places the page lists as incorporated, without dates

ledger.note: 1335: the dynasty's start year (infobox 1335-1381; 'ruled a state spanning central and eastern Anatolia from 1335 to 1381'). 'With Abu Sa'id's death in 1335, the Ilkhanid period practically came to an end'; Eretna, Timurtash's man and an Ilkhanid governor, took the Anatolian lands, 'under the suzerainty of the Jalayirid viceroy of Anatolia, Hasan Buzurg'. The land is the page's list of incorporated places, undated.
1338-1339: 'In 1338-1339, Eretna lost Darende to Qaraja' (the Dulkadir founder, who 'was continuing to enlarge his realm at the expanse of Eretna'). The page gives a two-year span; 1338 is used.

region.text: Erzincan with Erzurum and Bayburt: the eastern part of the realm

ledger.counterpart: Mongol warlords competing to restore the Ilkhanate (Hasan Kuchak's army under Suleiman Khan)
ledger.note: September-October 1343: 'After an unexpected victory at the Battle of Karanbük, against Mongol warlords competing to restore the Ilkhanate'; 'This victory resulted in the Eretnid annexation of Erzincan and several cities further east'. Hasan Kuchak 'dispatched his army to Anatolia under Suleiman Khan's command'. The cities beyond Erzincan are not named at this point; Erzurum and Bayburt are drawn from the later Ahi Ayna sentence.
1350: 'Eretna further took advantage of the Karamanid ruler Ahmed's death in 1350, capturing Konya.'
Page silent: the page does not say when the Karamanids regained Konya; placed at Eretna's death (1352) as a bridge. The beylik-of-karaman dossier has no Konya loss before 1390.
'The capital initially situated in Sivas and later Kayseri' (Eretnids page): the move is undated; placed at the accession of Muhammad I (1352), who was murdered 'in Kayseri, the capital'.

1361: 'In 1361, as a reprisal to a raid by Tatars of the Chavdar tribe', 'Ottoman ruler Murad I captured Ankara Castle from the Eretnids.' The ottoman-empire dossier has Ankara arriving in 1363 from the Ahi Republic.

region.text: Erzincan with Erzurum and Bayburt: the eastern part of the realm

ledger.counterpart: Ahi Ayna (local ruler of Erzincan, Erzurum and Bayburt)
ledger.note: About 1365: 'the eastern part of the realm, including Erzincan, Erzurum, and Bayburt, had come under the rule of a local figure, Ahi Ayna'. The year is the page's approximate date for the passage after Muhammad's death.

Page silent on the year: 'The Karamanids invaded Niğde and Aksaray, and local Mongol tribes started disrupting the public order', placed after Muhammad's death in 1365. The page says 'invaded', not that the towns were kept.

1375: 'Alaeddin Bey of the Karamanids seized Kayseri, forcing Alaeddin Ali to flee to Sivas' (Kadi Burhan al-Din page); 'the Karamanids captured the city with the help of the Mongol tribes of Samargar and Chaykazan' (Eretnids page).
1375: Alaeddin Ali flees from Kayseri to Sivas.
1378: 'Burhan al-Din reclaimed Kayseri and expelled Alaeddin Karamanid.'
The court returns to Kayseri with the city (page silent on the court; Ali still reigned until August 1380).

1381: 'In 1381, he took over Eretnid lands and claimed the title of sultan for himself.' The Eretnids page: Ali died in August 1380; the regent Kadi Burhan al-Din 'proclaimed himself as the ruler by January 1381'. Hajji Shadgeldi held Amasya against him until Burhan's victory later in 1381 (see the burhan-al-din-state dossier).

wars.name: Battle of Karanbük
belligerents: Hasan Kuchak (Chobanids), army under Suleiman Khan
wars.outcome: Eretna won on the plain of Karanbük, between Sivas and Erzincan, in September-October 1343 and annexed Erzincan and cities further east; the victory also began his independent reign (he had first used the title sultan on his coins in 1341).

wars.name: Dulkadir conquest of Darende
wars.outcome: Qaraja took Darende from Eretna in 1338-1339.

wars.name: Eretnid-Dulkadir campaign against the Mamluks at Malatya
wars.outcome: Muhammad I 'allied himself with the Dulkadirids in September 1362 in a joint campaign successfully driving the Mamluks from Malatya'; the page adds that 'this effort failed to regain Mamluk control' and does not say which of the allies kept the town.

wars.name: Karamanid invasion of Kayseri
wars.outcome: The Karamanids took Kayseri in 1375 and Burhan al-Din took it back in 1378.

certainty.note: The page lists the realm's places without dates; only Darende (1338), Erzincan (1343), Konya (1350), Ankara (1361), the east (about 1365) and Kayseri (1375, 1378) are dated. Provincial outlines stand in for towns and districts, so every frontier is an approximation.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Two pages opened (Eretnids, Kadi Burhan al-Din), within budget. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Territory: the Eretnids page gives a list of places 'incorporated' without dates, plus an extent 'from Konya to Ankara and Erzurum'. The 1335 keyframe draws the undated places from the first year; only Darende, Erzincan and the east, Konya, Ankara, the east again, Niğde and Aksaray, and Kayseri move on the dated sentences. Canik is drawn as a 40 km disc at Samsun, Şebinkarahisar as a 30 km disc, Darende as a 30 km disc; Develi and Zile fall inside Kayseri and Tokat provinces; the page's 'Karahisar' is not placed.
Status: the page puts Eretna under 'the suzerainty of the Jalayirid viceroy of Anatolia, Hasan Buzurg', who 'officially appointed' him governor; Eretna 'forged an alliance with the Mamluks, who confirmed him as the Mamluk governor of Anatolia'; he 'first declared his independence in 1341'. These are suzerain-side vassal events (jalayirid-sultanate, mamluk-sultanate): no dates beyond 1341, so none is recorded here.
Conflicts between the pages: capital Sivas then Kayseri (Eretnids) versus 'initial capital ... was Erzincan, later moving to Kayseri' (Kadi Burhan al-Din); Eretna's death 'February, March, or August 1352'; the Eretnids page also says 'Muhammad was killed by Kadi Burhan al-Din in 1390', a date that sits oddly against Burhan's own 1381 accession; the page also says a ruler was 'deposed by his emirs in 1354, and his half-brother Jafar reigned for a year (until 1355)', without naming the ruler: the ruler strip follows the infobox 1335-1352 and the 1365 murder only.
Mirrors the other dossiers lack: ottoman-empire carries Ankara in 1363 from the 'ahi-republic' (this page: Murad I took it from the Eretnids in 1361); beylik-of-karaman has no 1350 loss of Konya, no 1375 gain of Kayseri and no 1378 loss; beylik-of-dulkadir has no Darende gain in 1338-1339; chobanids carries no Karanbük; jalayirid-sultanate and mamluk-sultanate have no Eretna vassal events.
Not settled: whether Niğde and Aksaray were kept by the Karamanids after the invasion; what Erzincan, Erzurum and Bayburt did after Ahi Ayna (the page says 'Ali took advantage of the death of Pir Husayn Beg, Emir of Erzincan' in 1379 and gives no result); who kept Malatya in 1362.
Gazetteer names used that it may lack: Şebinkarahisar (place).
